## TL;DR

Added a standing rule that a task must not silently build user-visible UI its body does not name. The rule lives in three places: a one-line entry in `AGENTS.md`, a long-form section in `docs/agent-workflow-rules.md` that carries the #1189 and #1259 examples, and two built-in prompts in `DEFAULT_AGENTS` (`src/core/config.ts`). The engineer prompt says to flag needs-input with a proposal and stop before building. The reviewer prompt says to list unrequested UI as blocking under Bugs for a human to confirm. Prompt tests in `default-agent-prompts.test.ts` pin the wording. No `repoos.toml` change was needed or made.

## Work and rationale

The task asked for four things: an AGENTS.md rule, a long-form doc with the two examples, reviewer and engineer prompt text with tests, and QA-pass guidance. I kept the rule in one prompt location per role. The reviewer and engineer text live in `DEFAULT_AGENTS` in `src/core/config.ts`, which is where the task's "default agent prompt text" actually is. `reviewMission` in `src/server/review.ts` embeds the reviewer role text verbatim, so a reviewer pass gets the new bullet without a second copy.

The engineer instruction tells the engineer to flag the task with `repoos update <id> --needs-input true --questions "<the proposal>"`, not hand off, and end the turn. That matches the existing blocked-run guidance: leave the task active and stop. The reviewer instruction names the rule as blocking under Bugs and says the reviewer does not approve the change. It is not gated on the bar, so it also applies on the light bar for P3 tasks, which is the intent of "report as blocking".

For QA passes, no QA task template exists in code. `docs/qa/` holds past pass write-ups, not templates. I put the QA guidance in the workflow doc section and in the engineer prompt sentence, so both the written rule and the agent that receives it say QA passes file proposals rather than build UI.

`repoos.toml` was not edited. The task notes said to ask the human to apply any text there, but the engineer and reviewer text is in `DEFAULT_AGENTS`, not in the repo's config, so there was nothing to ask about.

## Approaches tried

I first searched for a `default-agent-prompts.ts` module, since the task named a test file and I expected a matching source file. None exists. The prompt text is in `DEFAULT_AGENTS` in `config.ts`, and the test imports `DEFAULT_AGENTS` through `promptFor`. Editing there keeps prompts in one place and the existing tests cover them.

I considered a separate constant for the UI rule shared by the engineer and reviewer text. I dropped it. Each role's text sits in an existing string, and a shared constant would have spread one sentence across two prompt builders for little gain.

## Challenges and blockers

Stored agent rows win over defaults. `agentsForConfig` in `src/core/config.ts` returns the stored list unchanged when a repo has `[[agents]]`, and it re-seeds only the Ross guide. A repo that already stores engineer or reviewer instructions will keep the old text until someone updates that row. The new text reaches only repos that use the built-in defaults. This is a limit of the change, not a bug in it, and a human should decide whether to refresh stored rows. I have not changed that behavior.

## Key learnings

Prompt rules are easiest to keep honest when the test file asserts exact phrases from the role text. The new tests check the reviewer's "blocking" wording, the engineer's needs-input step, and the AGENTS.md anchor that links to the long-form section. The AGENTS.md size budget (30000 bytes) still passes at about 28 KB after the one-line addition.
